claims.statement: 404 guide covers FPT/GHEC/GHES, with DNS/custom-domain sections conditional to FPT/GHEC. It recommends checking githubstatus.com first; global hosted status is not proof of a GHES appliance's own availability or the target site's effective response.

DNS diagnostic references provider configuration and domain-management guide; browser cache clearing is suggested for private-site 404. Neither observation proves correct ownership, deployed content or authorized private reader access.

Guide focuses on lowercase index.html and rejects Index.html/index.HTML. Creation guide additionally permits index.md or README.md; do not impose HTML-only repository policy from the narrower troubleshooting wording.

Entry file belongs at selected source-branch/folder top level, or deployed Actions artifact top level and may be generated. Initial repository-existence bullet must be qualified by the explicitly permitted generated-artifact alternative.

Directory-contents advice says root without fully distinguishing repository root from selected source/artifact root; preserve more precise source-mode instructions rather than relocating every repository file.

Cloud custom-domain CNAME points to user.github.io or organization.github.io without repository name. Landing page accessible with broken links may indicate custom-domain routing changes lacking rebuild; this is a possible diagnosis, not proven cause.

Source recommends automatic rebuild after domain add/remove, possibly modifying commit author and settings. Those changes are native mutations and do not constitute authorized remediation or observed successful rebuild.

Repository checklist says publishing branch must be main or default, conflicting with publishing-source reusable allowing any existing repository branch. Preserve conflict explicitly; no accepted main-only restriction or automatic branch rewrite.

Repository requires admin-pushed commit in this checklist; companion publishing guide additionally identifies verified email and GITHUB_TOKEN trigger exclusion. Admin role alone is insufficient evidence of effective build triggering.

Source claims changing repository public/private visibility changes Pages URL and requires rebuild; this broad statement remains unverified and must not be generalized to all site types. Repository visibility and private Pages reader visibility are distinct.

Private-repository guide suggests checking paid-plan activity, claims renewal auto-redeployment, and offers making repository public for free availability. Plan renewal can incur cost and public visibility can expose data; neither is authorized by this diagnostic guidance.

Community discussion is an escalation option, not authority to publish assessment details or an actual support/acceptance receipt. Full pinned article reviewed reference-only; no published assurance, adopted policy, rights clearance or native rollout certified.
